title: A line in the sand
told: a saying of the Prophet ﷺ

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? when you’re lost, what do you usually do?
options: fair. today, what happens when the phone runs out.
ha. i’ve done that too. today, a better way.

steps.line: A companion named Ibn Mas‘ud remembered a day when the Prophet ﷺ sat with them and began to draw in the sand.
First he drew one straight line. “This is the path of God,” he said.

steps.q: Then he drew more lines, branching off to the left and right. What do you think they were?
o: Other paths, each with a caller
steps.why: Other paths. On each one, a voice calling you to step onto it.

steps.line: Then lines to the right and left. “These are paths,” he said, “and on each one is a shaytan, a tempter, calling to it.”

steps.q: Why draw the crooked lines at all, instead of only the straight one?
o: They all lead to the same place in the end
Seeing the side roads makes the choice real
The drawing was easier to remember
steps.why: A straight line means little until you see what bends away. The choice is real, and so is the call.

steps.line: Then he recited from the Qur’an: “This is My straight path, so follow it, and don’t follow other ways, or they will scatter you.”
Al-Fatiha asks for exactly this: “Show us the straight path, the path of those You have blessed.” A road with footprints already on it.

steps.q: Al-Fatiha is recited in every unit of prayer. Across the five daily prayers, how many times a day is that, at least?
steps.why: Seventeen: once in every rak‘ah of the five prayers. The one request, “show us the straight path,” at least seventeen times a day.

steps.line: Ihdina, show us, guide us, comes from the root h-d-y. The same root gives hadiya, a gift. Guidance is something handed to you.

steps.q: Al-Fatiha asks for “the path of those You have blessed.” Another verse names them. Who are they?
o: The kings and scholars of old
steps.why: Qur’an 4:69: the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous, “and what excellent companions they are.” The road has footprints on it.

steps.line: Today, lost in a strange city, phone at two percent, you finally stop someone and ask: which way? Al-Fatiha asks that in every prayer.
steps.label: today

say: here’s what i love. the prophet ﷺ didn’t give a lecture. he drew one line in the sand, and everyone could see it.
in islam, the one thing al-fatiha asks for is guidance. and it says “us,” even when you pray alone at three in the morning.

steps.q: Even someone praying completely alone says “show us,” not “show me.” From this lesson, why?
o: The road is walked together, then and now
It’s just a polite way of saying me
The angels are saying it with you
steps.why: The path of those You have blessed. You never walk this road as the first or the only one.

today.say: today, before one choice, big or small, ask the question al-fatiha asks: which way? many muslims pause on that line in prayer: ihdina s-sirata l-mustaqim, show us the straight path. it’s your choice: just notice the line, learn it, or ask it yourself.
options: lovely. it’s waiting in every prayer.
I’ll ask it before a choice
beautiful. which way is a brave little question.

card.from: a saying of the Prophet ﷺ
sources: Musnad Ahmad 4142 (Ibn Mas‘ud: the Messenger of Allah drew a line and said “This is the path of Allah,” then drew lines to its right and left and said “These are paths, on each of which is a devil calling to it,” then recited 6:153); also Sunan ad-Darimi and an-Nasa’i, al-Sunan al-Kubra
Qur’an 6:153 (“This is My straight path, so follow it. Follow not other ways, lest ye be parted from His way,” Pickthall), paraphrased
Qur’an 1:6-7 (“Show us the straight path, the path of those whom Thou hast favoured”)
Root h-d-y (hidaya, guidance; hadiya, gift): Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon
check: The hadith is outside Bukhari and Muslim; it is graded hasan or sahih by later scholars (al-Hakim, Ahmad Shakir). Confirm the reference numbers.
